GRANTS OF OPTIONS AND AWARDS
This announcement is made by the Company pursuant to Rules 17.06A, 17.06B and 17.06C of the 
Listing Rules.
The Board hereby announces that on September 1, 2026, the Company granted (i) 2,040,450 
Options to 4 Grantees, and (ii) 306,749 Awards to 1 Grantee pursuant to the 2025 Share Incentive 
Plan (together, the “Grant”), representing approximately 0.30% and 0.05% of the total Shares in

(ii) breach of a fiduciary duty, or commission of a crime (other than

(c) a grantee has engaged in any act or omission to perform his/her

(d) the award to the grantee will no longer be appropriate and aligned

REASONS FOR AND BENEFITS OF THE GRANT
The purposes of the Grant are to (i) provide the Grantees with an opportunity to acquire proprietary 
interests in the Company; (ii) retain key personnel and high performers of the Group; (iii) provide 
the Grantees with additional incentives to achieve individual and corporate performance targets; 
and (iv) align the interests of the Grantees with those of the Shareholders by motivating them to 
enhance the value of the Company through equity ownership.
In particular, the Directors believe that, as a Service Provider Participant, Dr. Surmont’s extensive 
experience in the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries will be invaluable to the Group in 
advancing the commercialization of its core pipeline for the treatment of CKM diseases. The 
Directors further consider that the grant of Options to Dr. Surmont will assist the Company in 
retaining him as its chief medical officer and will incentivize him to contribute to the long-term 
growth and development of the Group, which aligns with the purpose of the 2025 Share Incentive 
Plan.

UPDATE ON CONNECTED TRANSACTION
TERMINATION OF THE LOAN AGREEMENT
Reference is made to the announcement of HighTide Therapeutics, Inc. (the “Company”) dated 
April 27, 2026 (the “Announcement”) in relation to the connected transaction regarding the Loan 
Agreement. Unless otherwise specified, capitalized terms used herein shall have the same meanings 
as those defined in the Announcement.
TERMINATION OF THE LOAN AGREEMENT
The Board hereby announces that on July 2, 2026, the Company (as the lender) and Dr. LIU 
Liping (“Dr. Liu”) (as the Borrower) have mutually agreed to terminate the Loan Agreement 
with immediate effect and the parties have unconditionally discharged each other from their 
obligations under the Loan Agreement. No amount under the facility has been drawn down prior to 
the termination of the Loan Agreement. The Directors consider that the termination will have no 
material adverse effect on the business and operations of the Group.
VIEWS OF THE STOCK EXCHANGE
As disclosed in the Announcement, as the highest applicable percentage ratio for the transaction 
contemplated under the Loan Agreement exceeds 0.1% but is less than 5%, the transaction is 
subject to the reporting and announcement requirements, but is exempt from the circular and 
independent shareholders’ approval requirements pursuant to Rule 14A.76(2) of the Listing Rules 
(the “Partial Exemption”).
Rule 14A.76(2) of the Listing Rules states that the Partial Exemption from the circular (including 
independent financial advice) and independent shareholders’ approval requirements applies to a 
connected transaction conducted on normal commercial terms or better.
When determining the interest rate of the facility, the Company used HIBOR (which represents a 
base lending rate between commercial banks and prime borrowers in Hong Kong) as a benchmark 
in determining the interest rate applicable to the facility, plus a margin reflecting an additional risk 
premium, and at the time, considered the reference to HIBOR to be consistent with precedent cases 
of other Hong Kong listed issuers.

[PDF PAGE 2]
2
Subsequent to the Announcement, the Stock Exchange has raised its concerns to the Company 
that the facility may not be on normal commercial terms or better, and accordingly, the Partial 
Exemption should not have been applied to the facility and the transaction contemplated 
thereunder should have been subject to the circular, independent financial advice and independent 
shareholders’ approval requirements under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules, for the reasons 
summarized below:
(a) the provision of the facility is outside the ordinary and usual course of business of the 
Company as a pre-revenue biotech company. The Stock Exchange considered that the specific 
risk profiles of Dr. Liu as a borrower and the Company itself as a lender were inherently 
higher than those of a prime borrower and a commercial bank respectively. Benchmarking 
with other market precedents would not be an appropriate approach to address the Stock 
Exchange’s concerns;
(b) the Stock Exchange also considered that the Borrower has yet to demonstrate that an 
unsecured personal loan on comparable terms would be available from independent 
commercial lender; and
(c) the Stock Exchange’s concern was further complicated by the fact that the facility carries 
minimal or no spread with reference to the Company’s cost of borrowings.
Accordingly, the Company should have complied with the following Listing Rules on a timely 
basis:
(a) Rule 14A.36 of the Listing Rules requires that a connected transaction must be conditional 
on shareholders’ approval at a general meeting held by the listed issuer. Any shareholder who 
has a material interest in the transaction must abstain from voting on the resolution;
(b) Rule 14A.39 of the Listing Rules requires an issuer to set up an independent board 
committee and appoint an independent financial advisor if the connected transaction requires 
shareholders’ approval; and
(c) Rule 14A.46 of the Listing Rules requires an issuer to send a circular to its shareholders if 
the connected transaction is to be approved by its shareholders in a general meeting.

[PDF PAGE 3]
3
RESPONSES FROM THE COMPANY
The Company attaches the utmost importance to compliance with the Listing Rules and all 
applicable laws and regulations. In light of the concern from the Stock Exchange, the parties have 
terminated the Loan Agreement, and no amount under the facility has been drawn down. Neither 
the interests of the Company nor those of the Shareholders have been prejudiced. The Company 
will comprehensively review and enhance its internal policies and procedures, so that the Directors, 
senior management and responsible personnel can make appropriate judgments on potential Listing 
Rules issues, and if necessary, escalate to the Board and/or seek professional advice on a timely 
basis.
By order of the Board
HighTide Therapeutics, Inc.
Dr. LIU Liping
Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer
Hong Kong, July 2, 2026
As at the date of this announcement, the Board comprises Dr. LIU Liping and Ms. YU Meng 
as executive Directors; Dr. ZHU Xun, Mr. MA Lixiong and Mr. JIANG Feng as non-executive 
Directors; and Dr. LI Jin, Mr. HUNG Tak Wai and Mr. CHEN Mingyu as independent 
non-executive Directors.

1. LISTING RULES
The Listing Rules permit a company whose primary listing is on the Stock Exchange to
repurchase its shares on the Stock Exchange and any other stock exchange on which the
securities of the company are listed and such exchange is recognized by the SFC and the Stock
Exchange subject to certain restrictions. Among such restrictions, the Listing Rules provide
that the shares of such company must be fully paid up and all repurchase of shares by such
company must be approved in advance by an ordinary resolution of Shareholders, either by way
of a general repurchase mandate or by specific approval of a particular transaction.
2. SHARE CAPITAL

resolution granting the Repurchase Mandate and on the basis that no further Shares are issued
or repurchased after the Latest Practicable Date and up to the Annual General Meeting, the

ending on the earliest of (i) the conclusion of the next annual general meeting of the Company;
(ii) the expiration of the period within which the next annual general meeting of the Company
is required to be held under any applicable laws or the Articles of Association; or (iii) the
revocation or variation of the authority given under the resolution by an ordinary resolution of
the Shareholders of the Company in general meeting.
3. STATUS OF REPURCHASED SHARES
The Shares repurchased by the Company may be held as treasury shares or may be
cancelled subject to, among others, market conditions and its capital management needs at the
relevant time of the repurchases, which may change due to evolving circumstances. The
Shareholders and potential investors should pay attention to any announcement to be published
by the Company in the future, including but without limitation, any next day disclosure return

treasury or cancelled upon settlement of such repurchases) and relevant monthly return.
For any treasury shares of the Company deposited with CCASS pending resale on the
Stock Exchange, the Company shall, upon approval by the Board implement the below interim
measures which include (without limitation):

for the treasury shares deposited with CCASS;

4. REASONS FOR AND FUNDING OF REPURCHASES
The Board believes that it is in the best interests of the Company and the Shareholders

funding arrangements at the time, lead to an enhancement of the net value of the Company
and/or its earnings per Share and will only be made when the Board believes that such
repurchase will be to the benefit of the Company and the Shareholders as a whole.
The Board proposes that the repurchase of Shares under the Repurchase Mandate would
be financed from internal resources of the Company. It is envisaged that the funds required for
any repurchase would be derived from the capital paid up on the Shares being repurchased and
from the distributable profits of the Company, as well as any funds legally available for such
purposes in accordance with the Company’s Articles of Association, the Cayman Companies

repurchase may be paid out of the profits of the Company or the proceeds of a fresh issue of

THE LOAN AGREEMENT
On April 27, 2026, the Company entered into the Loan Agreement with the Borrower, pursuant 
to which the Company agreed to make available to the Borrower the Loan in the maximum 
facility amount of HK$15,000,000.
IMPLICATIONS UNDER THE LISTING RULES
As of the date of this announcement, the Borrower is the founder, chairwoman of the Board, 
executive Director and chief executive officer of the Company. Accordingly, the Borrower 
is a connected person of the Company pursuant to Rule 14A.07 of the Listing Rules, and the 
transaction contemplated under the Loan Agreement constitutes a connected transaction for the 
Company pursuant to Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules. As the highest applicable percentage 
ratio for the transaction contemplated under the Loan Agreement exceeds 0.1% but is less 
than 5%, the transaction is subject to the reporting and announcement requirements, but is 
exempt from the circular and independent shareholders’ approval requirements pursuant to Rule 
14A.76(2) of the Listing Rules.
INTRODUCTION
On April 27, 2026, the Company entered into the Loan Agreement with the Borrower, pursuant to 
which the Company agreed to make available to the Borrower the Loan in the maximum facility 
amount of HK$15,000,000.

[PDF PAGE 2]
2
THE LOAN AGREEMENT
The principal terms of the Loan Agreement are as follows:
Date : April 27, 2026
Lender : The Company
Borrower : Dr. LIU Liping
Maximum Facility 
 Amount
: HK$15,000,000, being the maximum facility amount, which may 
be drawn down by the Borrower in one or more tranches at the 
Borrower’s sole discretion
Term of the Loan : The Loan is repayable in full on the first anniversary of the first 
drawdown date, provided that if, on or before such date, (i) the 
Borrower has paid in full all accrued interest up to such date; and 
(ii) upon written request from the Borrower, the term of the Loan 
shall be extended for an additional one-year period, in which case 
the final repayment date shall be the second anniversary of the 
first drawdown date
Drawdown Date: : In respect of each drawdown, drawdown date means the date on 
which such tranche of the Loan is actually made available and 
drawn down by the Borrower, and the Borrower may make one or 
more drawdowns in tranches within 180 days following the date 
of the Loan Agreement
Interest Rate : 3.50 per cent. (3.50%) per annum. Interest shall accrue on the 
outstanding principal amount of the Loan actually drawn down on 
the basis of the actual number of days elapsed and a 365-day year, 
for each drawdown, from and including its respective drawdown 
date to but excluding the date of actual repayment, and shall be 
calculated on a simple (non-compounding) basis
Purpose of the Loan : For the Borrower’s tax compliance purpose
Type of the Loan : Unsecured loan
Interest Payment Dates : On the anniversary of the first drawdown date, the Borrower shall 
pay all accrued interest up to such date. If the term of the Loan is 
extended for another one-year period in accordance with the Loan 
Agreement, all accrued interest for the extended period shall be 
payable on the expiry date of the extended term
Early Repayment : The Borrower may, upon giving prior notice, elect to prepay the 
Loan in full or in part prior to the expiry of the Loan term. In 
the event of such prepayment, interest shall be calculated based 
on the actual number of days during which the Loan remained 
outstanding

[PDF PAGE 3]
3
To ensure ongoing oversight, the finance department of the Company will be primarily responsible 
for monitoring the Borrower’s repayment of the Loan (including any interest payment) and will 
report the status of the Loan at least annually until the Loan is fully repaid. In the event of a 
default, the Company reserves the right to demand immediate repayment and apply a default 
interest rate of 8% per annum on any outstanding balance.
REASONS FOR AND BENEFITS OF ENTERING INTO THE LOAN AGREEMENT
The terms of the Loan Agreement, including the maximum facility amount and interest rate, were 
determined after arm’s length negotiations between the Company and the Borrower. In arriving at 
these terms, the parties took into account the prevailing market interest rates, terms and practices. 
The Company intends to fund the Loan using its internal resources.
The Company entered into the Loan Agreement after considering the following factors: (i) the 
Group’s latest financial position and the availability of internal resources; (ii) the Loan will not 
adversely affect the Group’s working capital or its day-to-day operations; and (iii) the interest 
income generated by the Loan is expected to exceed the Group’s funding costs and the interest 
income from time deposits of a comparable term.
Further, the Company (with the coordination of the finance department and human resources 
department) conducted a comprehensive assessment of the Borrower’s repayment capacity, taking 
into account: (i) the Borrower’s current and expected remuneration, alongside the potential 
realizable value of share awards scheduled to vest during the Loan term; (ii) the prevailing market 
value of securities held by the Borrower; (iii) the Borrower’s long-term service with the Group 
as well as her sound integrity record, historical performance and commitment to the Group; and 
(iv) the Loan was intended for legitimate tax compliance purpose. Based on the results of the 
aforementioned assessment, the Board (excluding the Borrower, who has abstained from voting 
on the relevant resolution) is satisfied that the Borrower possesses sufficient repayment capacity 
and a bona fide intention to perform her obligations under the Loan Agreement, particularly given 
that her interests are closely aligned with the long-term success of the Company. Accordingly, the 
Board concluded that the overall risk associated with the Loan is relatively low, and expected the 
Borrower to fulfill the repayment of the principal and all accrued interest in strict accordance with 
the terms of the Loan Agreement.
In view of the above, the Directors (including the independent non-executive Directors) consider 
that the terms of the Loan Agreement are fair and reasonable, and although the transaction 
contemplated under the Loan Agreement is not in the ordinary and usual course of business of 
the Group, it is on normal commercial terms or better and in the interests of the Company and its 
shareholders taken as a whole.

HIGHTIDE THERAPEUTICS ANNOUNCES ACCEPTANCE OF NEW

This announcement is made by HighTide Therapeutics, Inc. (the “Company”, together with its 
subsidiaries, the “Group”) on a voluntary basis to inform the shareholders and potential investors 
of the Company about the latest business development of the Group.
The board of directors (the “Board”) of the Company announces that the National Medical 
Products Administration (NMPA) of China has accepted the New Drug Application (NDA) 
for HTD1801 for the treatment of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). This marks the first 
NDA submitted by HighTide Therapeutics and a major milestone on its path towards product 
commercialization.
HTD1801 has completed three multicenter, randomized, double-blind, controlled Phase III clinical 
trials for the T2DM indication – all of which met their primary endpoints as well as multiple 
secondary endpoints. Across these studies, HTD1801 consistently demonstrated improvements in 
multiple dimensions of the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) spectrum, including glycemic 
control, lipid metabolism, inflammatory markers, and renal function. These results highlight the 
potential of HTD1801 to deliver comprehensive, multi-system therapeutic benefits through a single 
therapy.

on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited: The Company cannot guarantee that HTD1801 
will ultimately be successfully marketed. Shareholders and potential investors of the Company are 
advised to exercise caution when dealing in the shares of the Company.
